# Introduction

Here we use the Holland wind model to illustrate the radial wind
profile of a hypothetical hurricane.

# Holland wind profile

The Holland model describes the radial variation in wind speed around
a tropical cyclone. For this example, we use hypothetical storm
parameters.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Hypothetical hurricane parameters
P_c = 950       # central pressure (hPa)
P_n = 1010      # ambient pressure (hPa)
R_max = 40      # radius of maximum wind (km)
B = 1.5         # Holland B parameter
rho = 1.15      # air density (kg/m^3)

# Radius from storm center
r = np.linspace(1, 200, 500)

# Convert radius to meters
r_m = r * 1000
R_max_m = R_max * 1000

# Pressure difference
delta_P = (P_n - P_c) * 100  # hPa -> Pa

# Holland wind-speed equation
V = np.sqrt(
    (B / rho) *
    delta_P *
    (R_max_m / r_m)**B *
    np.exp(-(R_max_m / r_m)**B)
)

# Plot
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
plt.plot(r, V, linewidth=2)

plt.axvline(
    R_max,
    color="red",
    linestyle="--",
    label="Radius of maximum wind"
)

plt.xlabel("Radius from storm center (km)")
plt.ylabel("Wind speed (m/s)")
plt.title("Hypothetical Hurricane: Holland Wind Profile")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Results

The resulting curve shows how the modeled wind speed varies with
distance from the hurricane center. The maximum occurs near the
specified radius of maximum wind.
